instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch cubes. Dice the onion. Mince the garlic. Chop 1/2 cup of the cilantro.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and half of the chopped cilantro. Cook for 1 minute, until the cilantro wilts.
Stir in the ground coriander and the tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens a little.
Add the potatoes, 1 1/2 tsp of the salt, the black pepper and 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff it.
Drain and rinse the butter beans and add them to the stew. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when you pierce them with a fork.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the rest of the chopped cilantro. Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice with the other half of the lemon, cut into wedges.
To store, let the stew cool, then refrigerate it in a covered container for up to 5 days. Reheat only what you'll eat, in a pot over medium-low heat with a splash of water until it's steaming.
method_notes: The lead (Plant Based Folk, 5.0 from 99) simmers potatoes and butter beans with onion, garlic, cilantro and ground coriander, and serves it over grain. Its beans are dried and soaked 4 hours; canned beans are used here and go in for the last 10 minutes. Tomato paste comes from Zaatar and Zaytoun's yakhne to match the list's promise, since the lead has none. Served over rice rather than bulgur vermicelli to stay gluten-free. Vegan and gluten-free as written.
